input.quote: 15.16 Nonsolicitation. During the Term and for a period of [***] thereafter, neither Party shall solicit an employee of the other Party who is or has been involved in the performance or oversight of any of the development activities hereunder to terminate his or her employment and accept employment or work as a consultant with the soliciting Party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing herein shall restrict or preclude the Parties' right to make generalized searches for employees by way of a general solicitation for employment placed in a trade journal, newspaper or website.
input.rationale: Section 15.16 is the only non-solicitation provision in the agreement and it binds PB as well as SFJ. It already satisfies several fallback elements: it is mutual, it reaches only personnel involved in the performance or oversight of the development activities, it bars solicitation only (no no-hire), and it carves out general solicitations placed in a trade journal, newspaper or website. It fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) the duration runs for the whole Term plus an undisclosed ([***]) tail measured from expiry rather than 12 months from the end of the individual's involvement, so it can bind PB far longer than the fallback allows; and (ii) there is no carve-out for employees who approach a Party on an unsolicited basis. The redline makes the shortest edits to fix duration and add the unsolicited-approach carve-out, leaving the mutual, involvement-limited, solicitation-only structure intact.

proposal.summary: Cap the non-solicit at 12 months after the individual's involvement ends and add an unsolicited-approach carve-out.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can accept a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the development activities, but the duration must run for no more than 12 months after that individual's involvement ends rather than the Term plus an undisclosed tail, and hires resulting from unsolicited approaches must be carved out alongside general advertisements.

ops.oldText: During the Term and for a period of [***] thereafter, neither Party shall solicit an employee of the other Party who is or has been involved in the performance or oversight of any of the development activities hereunder
ops.newText: Neither Party shall, until twelve (12) months after an employee of the other Party ceases to be involved in the performance or oversight of any of the development activities hereunder, solicit such employee

ops.oldText: Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing herein shall restrict or preclude the Parties' right to make generalized searches for employees by way of a general solicitation for employment placed in a trade journal, newspaper or website.
ops.newText: Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing herein shall restrict or preclude the Parties' right to make generalized searches for employees by way of a general solicitation for employment placed in a trade journal, newspaper or website, or to hire any employee who approaches a Party on an unsolicited basis.
